text:
alex: Hi team, first day trouble  running the repo's `./dev up` and postgres container exits instantly. Error in logs: `could not bind Unix socket \"/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432\": Permission denied`. On an M2 Mac + Docker Desktop. Any quick checks?

sam: Welcome! that usually means your compose is mounting a host dir over the socket dir. Can you paste the postgres service from your compose?

alex: this is the minimal snippet from `docker-compose.yml`:
```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    volumes:
      - ./pgdata:/var/run/postgresql
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: devpass
```

marie: yep that's it  you shouldn't bind to `/var/run/postgresql`. The socket dir is created by the container and needs specific ownership/SELinux bits sometimes. Mount your data under `/var/lib/postgresql/data` or use a named volume.

sam: on macos you also hit the Docker Desktop file sharing and permission mapping weirdness. If you insist on a host bind, do `mkdir -p pgdata && sudo chown -R 999:999 pgdata` (postgres uid 999) then switch to `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` in compose. But named volumes are simpler: `volumes: pgdata:` and `- pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`.

alex: I changed to `/var/lib/postgresql/data` and `chown` but my app still says `could not connect to server: No such file or directory` referencing `/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432`.

marie: that's because your client is trying to use a unix socket path on the host. In many setups `DATABASE_URL` or `PGHOST` falls back to a socket if host missing. Check your env: `env | grep PG` or `echo $DATABASE_URL`. For compose-based dev we prefer explicit TCP: set `DB_HOST=postgres` or `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:devpass@postgres:5432/redwood`.

sam: also make sure both services are on the same compose network (default is fine). Our `./dev` wrapper injects `DB_HOST=postgres` into the web service in `docker-compose.override.yml` if you use the script. If you run services manually, you might miss that override.

alex: I had `DATABASE_URL=postgres:///redwood` in my shell from a previous project, which explains the socket attempt. Removed it and used `postgresql://postgres:devpass@postgres:5432/redwood` and the web connected right away. Thanks!

marie: awesome. A few onboarding tips: 1) prefer named volumes to avoid host FS permission issues on macs, 2) explicitly set DB_HOST/PGHOST for dev to force TCP, 3) if you need host psql access map a different host port like `5433:5432` to avoid conflicts with a local postgres installation.

devops-bot: Note: dev checklist in repo `onboarding` has an entry about mac file sharing; maintainers welcome additions.

alex: I'll open an issue with the exact error and the fix I used (named volume + DB_HOST override) so future new hires can find it. Filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/issues/87 and linked this thread. Thanks everyone!! :sparkles:
